'''Tamaru-hime Falls''' (多留姫の滝, also 樽姫の滝) is a waterfall in {{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino City}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nagano|af|Nagano-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nagano|ar|ناغانو (محافظة)|arz|محافظه ناجانو|az|Naqano prefekturası|azb|ناقانو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nagano|be|Нагана (прэфектура)|bg|Нагано|bn|নাগানো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nagano|cdo|Nagano-gâing|ce|Нагано (префектура)|ceb|Nagano-ken|ckb|پارێزگای ناگانۆ|cs|Prefektura Nagano|cy|Nagano (talaith)|da|Nagano-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nagano|eo|Gubernio Nagano|es|Prefectura de Nagano|et|Nagano prefektuur|eu|Nagano (prefektura)|fa|استان ناگانو|fi|Naganon prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nagano|frr|Nagano (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nagano|gl|Prefectura de Nagano|hak|Nagano-yen|he|נאגנו (מחוז)|hr|Nagano (prefektura)|hu|Nagano prefektúra|hy|Նագանո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nagano|ilo|Prepektura ti Nagano|it|Prefettura di Nagano|ja|長野県|ka|ნაგანოს პრეფექტურა|kaa|Nagano prefekturası|kn|ನಾಗನೊ (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|나가노현|la|Naganoënsis|lt|Nagano prefektūra|lv|Nagano prefektūra|mk|Нагано (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯒꯥꯅꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नागानो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nagano|ne|नगानो|nl|Nagano (prefectuur)|no|Nagano (prefektur)|nov|Nagano Prefekture|os|Нагано (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nagano|pl|Prefektura Nagano|pnb|ضلع ناگانو|pt|Nagano|ro|Prefectura Nagano|ru|Нагано (префектура)|sco|Nagano Prefectur|se|Nagano prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nagano|si|නගානො ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nagano Prefecture|sk|Nagano (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nagano|sr|Префектура Нагано|su|Nagano Prefecture|sv|Nagano prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nagano|tg|Префектураи Нагано|th|จังหวัดนางาโนะ|tl|Prepektura ng Nagano|tr|Nagano (prefektörlük)|tt|Нагано (префектура)|uk|Нагано (префектура)|ur|ناگانو پریفیکچر|vi|Nagano|war|Nagano (prefektura)|wuu|长野县|zh|长野县|zh_classical|長野縣|zh_min_nan|Nagano-koān|zh_yue|長野縣|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}. It is also referred to as "Tamaru-hime Falls" in alternate kanji<ref name="chinoshishigekan">‘Chino City History: Modern and Folklore,’ pp. 1069–1070.</ref><ref>‘Chino City History: Supplement Natural History,’ p. 33.</ref>. The falls are designated as a cultural property by Chino City.

== Geography ==
'''Tamaru-hime Falls''' is located east of Chino City's central area, at the foot of [[Mount Oizumi]], along the [[Yanagawa (Nagano)|Yanagawa River]]. From the summit of Mount Oizumi, one can see {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|qid=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji}} to the left of [[:en:Mount Yatsugatake|Mount Yatsugatake]], with the falls visible below<ref name="choson_3351">‘Nagano Prefectural Town and Village Records: Chuo and Minami-Shin Regions,’ p. 3351.</ref>. The falls have an initial drop of 9 meters in height and width, followed by a right-angle turn with a 3-meter height and 1-meter width<ref name="taki100_120" />. The records describe the water flow as resembling a beaded curtain, producing a sound akin to a harp in the wind. Across the seasons, visitors can enjoy [[wisteria]] and [[:en:cuckoos|cuckoos]] in spring, cool retreats in summer, [[:en:autumn leaves|autumn leaves]], and {{ill|Snow|en|Snow|qid=Q7561|lt=Snow}} in winter<ref name="choson_3351" />. Downstream, the Yanakage and Nagare Bridges span the falls<ref name="kahimap">{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/3786.pdf |title=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park Monument Map |publisher=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park Creation Committee |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>, while the Tamaru-hime Bridge of [[Nagano Prefectural Route 17]] crosses the valley<ref>Geospatial Information Authority of Japan "[http://watchizu.gsi.go.jp/watchizu.html?longitude=138.21555558329&latitude=35.993490818409 Watchizu]" (Accessed May 26, 2012).</ref>.

Next to the falls is '''Tamaru-hime Shrine'''<ref name="taki100_120" />, dedicated to [[Tamaru-hime|Tamaru-hime-no-Kami]] (daughter of [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-Kami]], the deity of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]])<ref>‘Japanese Historical Place Names: Volume 20, Nagano Prefecture,’ p. 358.</ref>. While the shrine's founding date is unknown, it is documented to have existed over 750 years ago<ref name="taki100_120" />.

Chino City designated Tamaru-hime Falls as a cultural property on [[July 29, 1988]] (Showa 63)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/soshiki/bunkazai/1665.html |title=City Designated Cultural Properties |publisher=Chino City |date=2018-12-03 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>. The surrounding area, known as '''Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park''', is managed by a committee from local districts that maintains and hosts events<ref name="hp">{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/soshiki/shogaigakushu/851.html |title=Tamaru-hime Literature and Nature Park |publisher=Chino City |date=2019-12-20 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>. Various monuments inscribed with poems and haiku by notable figures, such as [[:en:Matsuo Basho|Matsuo Basho]], are found in the area, along with submission boxes for original works<ref name="kahimap" />. The park's mascot is '''Tamaru-hime-chan''', depicted sitting on a scroll in the falls' basin<ref name="hp" />. In 2014, to commemorate the park's 10th anniversary, a new mascot named '''Shion''' (紫音) was introduced, designed by local high school students<ref name="hp" /><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.nagano-np.co.jp/modules/news/article.php?storyid=31134 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517123128/http://www.nagano-np.co.jp/modules/news/article.php?storyid=31134 |title=Local Charm: Tamaru-hime Character Introduced by Chino Creation Committee to Promote the Falls |newspaper=[[Nagano Daily News]] |publisher=Nagano Newspaper |date=2014-04-18 |archivedate=2014-05-17 |accessdate=2020-01-03 }}</ref>.

== Legends ==
;{{ill|Lending Bowl Legend|ja|椀貸伝説}}
: A legend tells of Tamaru-hime lending bowls to villagers in need. The following summary is derived from ‘{{ill|Q97184907|ja|長野県史|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagano Prefectural History|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97184907}}’:
:: Long ago, a hardworking couple with a harmonious relationship was blessed with a child. Wanting to celebrate but unable to afford sufficient bowls for the guests, they dreamed of Tamaru-hime instructing them to write their needs on paper and drop it into the falls' basin. Upon doing so, the bowls appeared the next morning. After the celebration, the couple cleaned the bowls and returned them. However, a lazy villager, hearing of this, tried the same but kept one bowl, believing it wouldn't be noticed. Since then, Tamaru-hime ceased lending<ref>‘Nagano Prefectural History: Folklore Edition, Volume II (3),’ pp. 589–591.</ref>.
: Another version suggests that broken bowls caused Tamaru-hime to stop lending<ref name="chinoshishigekan" />.

== Access ==
;[[:en:Public Transportation|Public Transportation]]
: A short walk west from Tamaru-hime Shrine leads to Kizandō. Proceeding further brings you to [[Nagano Prefectural Route 188]] at Nakazawa Intersection, near Nakazawa Bus Stop<ref>"[http://www.mapion.co.jp/m/35.9901438_138.2181119_8/v=m5:%E5%A4%9A%E7%95%99%E5%A7%AB%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ Mapion Map: Tamaru-hime Shrine]" (Accessed May 31, 2012).</ref>. Take the Nakazawa Line bus from {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=East Japan Railway Company}}'s [[:en:Chuo Main Line|Chuo Main Line]] {{ill|Chino Station|en|Chino Station|qid=Q844063|lt=Chino Station}}, reaching Nakazawa in under 20 minutes<ref>Chino City "[http://www.city.chino.lg.jp/kbn/Files/1/01130262/attach/basurosenH24.4.28.pdf Chino City Bus Routes: Revised April 28, 2012]" (Accessed May 31, 2012).</ref>.
